### Specific API Error Handling

To handle specific HTTP errors like 404, 401, etc., you can extend the error handling further:

```javascript
async function fetchWeatherData() {
  try {
    const response = await fetch('https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather');
    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
    }
    const data = await response.json();
    // handle data
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error fetching weather data:', error);
    let errorMessage;
    if (error instanceof TypeError) {
      errorMessage = 'Network error occurred. Please check your internet connection.';
    } else if (error.message.includes('HTTP error')) {
      const status = parseInt(error.message.split(' ')[3]);
      switch (status) {
        case 404:
          errorMessage = 'The requested location was not found.';
          break;
        case 401:
          errorMessage = 'Invalid API key. Please check your API key.';
          break;
        case 429:
          errorMessage = 'Too many requests. Please try again later.';
          break;
        default:
          errorMessage = `API returned an error with status: ${status}`;
      }
    } else {
      errorMessage = 'An unexpected error occurred while fetching weather data.';
    }
    // display user-friendly error message
    alert(errorMessage);
  }
}
```

Here, we are checking the HTTP status code and providing specific messages for common errors like 404, 401, and 429. This will give users more context about what went wrong and how they might resolve it.
